zh.title: 華航首獲SGS隱私暨個資管理卓越獎　23家企業角逐僅2家獲獎
zh.summary: 中華航空首度獲得SGS 2026 DT Awards「隱私暨個資管理卓越獎」，為本屆唯一獲獎的航空公司。華航除通過兩項國際管理系統驗證，2025年民航局個資保護行政檢查亦獲零缺失。
body: 中華航空（China Airlines）11月5日宣布，首度獲頒SGS 2026 DT Awards「隱私暨個資管理卓越獎」，成為國內首家獲得此獎的航空公司。據華航說明，本屆共有23家企業角逐該獎項，最後僅2家獲獎，華航是其中唯一的航空業者。對需要處理大量旅客資料的航空公司而言，資訊安全與個人隱私管理已成為日常營運的重要環節。
這項獎項由國際檢驗與驗證機構SGS頒發。相關評選原於2019年以「IT Awards資訊治理卓越獎」之名舉辦，2026年改為「DT Awards數位信任與韌性獎」，關注企業在資訊安全、隱私保護及營運韌性等領域的管理表現。本次由SGS管理與保證事業群副總裁鮑柏宇頒發獎座，華航資安暨個資管理處處長何惠芬代表受獎。
華航表示，已將資訊安全及個人資料保護納入公司治理與風險管理架構，並取得ISO 27001資訊安全管理系統與ISO 27701隱私資訊管理系統兩項國際驗證。前者著重資訊安全管理制度及風險控管，後者則聚焦個人資料處理與隱私管理，讓航空公司能以制度化方式辨識、評估及管理相關風險。
這些規範並非只用於企業內部資訊系統。旅客從訂位、購票、辦理報到，到搭機期間接受服務，都可能涉及姓名、聯絡方式、旅行資料等資訊的處理。華航表示，已將相關管理要求納入上述旅客服務流程，讓個資保護涵蓋旅客與航空公司接觸的不同階段。
在實際管理作業方面，華航導入數位化個資管理系統，整合個資盤點、隱私衝擊評估及風險追蹤等功能。個資盤點用來掌握資料的持有與使用情況；隱私衝擊評估則協助辨識資料處理流程中可能產生的風險，並追蹤後續改善情形。華航稱，這套作法有助於提升作業效率與資料防護能力。
除國際驗證外，華航表示，2025年接受交通部民用航空局個資保護行政檢查，結果為零缺失。公司也透過定期稽核、應變演練與員工教育訓練，強化各部門對資料保護的認識與處理能力；相關管理要求並延伸至委外合作夥伴及跨境資料傳輸，降低資料在不同作業環節流通時的風險。
華航另指出，在2026年標普全球永續年鑑（S&P Global The Sustainability Yearbook）相關評比中，公司獲列全球前1%企業，並在全球航空業取得最高分；其中，隱私保護題組已連續兩年拿下滿分。上述成績為華航對外公布的評比結果，與本次SGS獎項屬不同評鑑制度。
面對旅客服務持續數位化，航空公司的資料管理範圍也逐漸從訂票及報到系統，延伸至合作廠商與跨境作業。華航表示，未來將逐步擴大ISO 27701國際驗證的涵蓋範圍，持續調整資安與隱私防護措施。對旅客而言，這些平時不易察覺的後端管理工作，也是評估航空服務可信賴程度的一環。

en.title: China Airlines wins SGS privacy management award as one of two winners from 23 contenders
en.summary: China Airlines has received the 2026 SGS DT Awards Privacy and Personal Data Management Excellence Award for the first time, becoming the only airline among two winners selected from 23 entrants. The carrier cites international certifications and a clean 2025 regulatory inspection.
body: China Airlines announced on November 5 that it had won the Privacy and Personal Data Management Excellence Award at the 2026 SGS DT Awards, its first recognition in this category. According to the Taiwanese carrier, 23 companies competed for the award and only two were selected. China Airlines was the sole airline among the recipients, highlighting the growing importance of protecting customer information throughout the passenger journey.

The awards are organized by SGS, an international testing, inspection and certification organization. The program began in 2019 as the IT Awards for information governance and was renamed the DT Awards for digital trust and resilience in 2026. It recognizes corporate practices involving information security, privacy and operational resilience. The award was presented by SGS executive Po-Yu Pao to China Airlines' information security and personal data management director, Hui-Fen Ho.

The airline says it has incorporated information security and the protection of personal data into its corporate governance and risk-management framework. It has obtained ISO 27001 certification for information security management and ISO 27701 certification for privacy information management. While the first standard addresses systematic management of information security risks, the second focuses on the governance of personal data processing and related privacy risks.

These policies extend beyond back-office systems. China Airlines says it applies privacy-related requirements to passenger reservations, ticket purchases, check-in and onboard services. Such operations may involve handling customers' names, contact details and travel information at several points, making consistent controls across different service stages particularly relevant.

The carrier has also introduced a digital personal-data management platform that combines data inventories, privacy impact assessments and risk tracking. In practical terms, those functions help the company identify the information it holds, assess privacy implications in workflows and monitor follow-up actions. China Airlines says this integration improves management efficiency and its ability to protect customer data.

China Airlines reported that a personal-data protection administrative inspection conducted by Taiwan's Civil Aviation Administration in 2025 identified no deficiencies. It also described regular audits, response exercises and staff training, with privacy-management requirements extending to outsourced partners and cross-border data transfers. These measures address risks that can arise when information moves between departments or service providers.

In a separate assessment, China Airlines said it was recognized among the global top 1% of companies in the 2026 S&P Global Sustainability Yearbook, achieved the highest score among airlines worldwide, and earned full marks for the privacy-protection category for two consecutive years. The S&P assessment and the SGS award are distinct recognition programs and should not be conflated.

Looking ahead, the airline plans to broaden the scope of its ISO 27701 certification and continue improving its information security and privacy controls. As more stages of air travel are handled digitally, the way airlines manage customer information, contractors and international data transfers remains an important part of maintaining passenger trust.
